newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's Credor to cede 15 pct of stock.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's Credor to cede 15 pct of stock.

text.p: Moroccan firm Credor, which was recently floated on the bourse, plans to cede 15 percent of its stock worth $14.1 million to strategic investors, broker Upline Securities said on Friday.

"Credor which controls 16 percent of the home appliances and personal loans market, plans to cede 15 percent of the company's capital worth 134 million dirhams at current market value to some strategic partners, including a local bank and insurance firm," Sofia Echihabi an analyst at the Casablanca- based Upline told Reuters.
No date for sale was set yet, the analyst said.

The decision is aimed at securing financial backing and expertise, she said. The company wants to diversify into life insurance and other assistance products as part of its meduim- term strategic policy, Echihabi said.
According to an Upline report, Credor financed 38,700 loans worth 467 million dirhams in 1996, up 29.2 percent over the previous year.

"Credor's net income rose 14.7 percent to 52.25 million dirhams in 1996 compared with 1995...It also showed a 27.3 percent return on equity, or one of the best performances in the sector," Upline said.

Upline expects positive prospects for Credor as "its total lending in 1997 should rise 28 percent to 600 million dirhams. This will come from a 20 percent increase in home appliances loans, while personal loans should almost double."

Credor has a market capitalisation of 925.2 million dirhams with an average daily trading volume of 2.1 million dirhams, it said. The firm, which has 1.2 million shares outstanding, was last traded at 752 dirhams, traders said.
